<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par113 />dition on which some consequence depends, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=26}} ''if thou wilt diligently hearken'', &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=19|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=22|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, 11 f. 16, 22 (see above, ''m''); 23:22, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=12|verse=25|hidebook=1}}; after {{GHGheb|text=לוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=30}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|p}}
The infinitive absolute is used to give emphasis to an antithesis, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=24|verse=24}} ''nay; but I will verily buy'' ({{GHGheb|text=קָנוֹ אֶקְנֶה}}) ''it of thee'', &c. (not receive it as a gift); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=15|verse=13}} ''no; but we will bind thee fast ... but surely we will not kill thee''; cf. further {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=30}} (thou art indeed gone=) ''though thou wouldst needs be gone'' (Vulg. ''esto''), ''because thou sore longedst'', &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=13}}, 18, 126:6 (the second infinitive absolute as a supplement to the first—see below, ''r''—comes ''after'' the verb).—Hence also, as permissive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=16}} f. {{GHGheb|text=אָכֹל תֹּאכֵל|translate=thou mayest freely eat, but}}, &c. (so that verse 16 is in antithesis to verse 17); or concessive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=30}} ''I said indeed'' ..., 14:43.

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|q}}
The infinitive absolute is used to strengthen a question, and especially in impassioned or indignant questions, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=הֲמָלֹךְ תִּמְלֹךְ עָ֫לֵינוּ|translate=shalt thou indeed reign over us?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=43}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=28|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=3|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=7|verse=5}}; but cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=5}} ''must I needs bring again?''

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|r}}
(''b'') The infinitive absolute ''after the verb'', sometimes (as in ''n'') to intensify<ref>In Arabic also, the intensifying infinitive regularly stands ''after'' the verb, but in Syriac ''before'' the verb.</ref> the idea of the verb (especially after imperatives and participles, since the infinitive absolute can never precede either, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=37|verse=2|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=שִׁמְעוּ שָׁמוֹעַ|translate=hearken ye attentively}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=10}}; after participles, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=17}}, also elsewhere, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=24|verse=10|hidebook=1}} ''thou hast altogether blessed them''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=24|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=11|verse=10}}, and with the infinitive absolute strengthened by means of {{GHGheb|text=גַּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=46|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=16|verse=13}}); sometimes to express the long ''continuance'' of an action; here again after an imperative, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=שִׁמְעוּ שָׁמוֹעַ|translate=hear ye continually}}; after a perfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=29}}; after a participle, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=17}}; after an imperfect consecutive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=32}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|s}}
To this class belong especially those cases in which a second infinitive absolute is co-ordinated with the first; the latter then expresses either an accompanying or antithetical action or the aim to which the principal action is directed; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=הָֽלְכוּ הָלֹךְ וְגָעוֹ|translate=lowing as they went}} (lowing continually; so after a participle, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=6|verse=13}}b {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=7}} ''it went forth to and fro''<ref>Also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=1|verse=14}} for the distorted form {{GHGheb|text=רצוא}} reads simply {{GHGheb|text=יָֽצְאוּ יָצוֹא}}.</ref>; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=22}} ''smiting and'' (i.e. but also) ''healing again''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=2|verse=26}} (see above, ''m'').

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|t}}
Rem. 1. Instead of a second infinitive absolute (see above) there is sometimes found a perfect consecutive (Jos. 6:13 a and {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=19}} [but Stade’s {{GHGheb|text=וְזָעוֹק}} is<section end=par113 /><noinclude>
